newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Work still needed on Israel-PLO deal-Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Work still needed on Israel-PLO deal-Netanyahu.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday after talks with King Hussein of Jordan that more work was needed to achieve a deal with the PLO on more Israeli troop withdrawals from the West Bank.

"I think because of the important initiative that His Majesty took we have made considerable progress and I think we can envision the end of the negotiations in sight. There is still work to be done but I think we've made a very important step forward," Netanyahu told a news conference.

Earlier, PLO officials said King Hussein was carrying a compromise proposal to Netanyahu on a new timeframe for three Israeli troop redeployments to follow a still unimplemented army pullback from the West Bank town of Hebron, a flashpoint of Arab-Israeli violence.

U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross, who has been trying to broker a deal, said he had planned to return to the United States on Sunday but President Bill Clinton had asked him to stay "because of the progress that was made today". He said "the differences are not great" between the parties but he gave no details.
Ross arrived three weeks ago to try again to forge a deal to launch Palestinian self-rule in 80 percent of Hebron.

King Hussein, who flew to Tel Aviv from Gaza where he met Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, said at the news conference: "I believe...we are on the verge of the completion of a long road and as far as I'm concerned, I leave here confident that everything will move in the right direction."
Earlier Jordanian Information Minister Marwan Muasher told reporters: "The (Arafat-King Hussein) meeting was very successful."
"We had several contacts with Egyptian President (Hosni) Mubarak, (U.S. Secretary of State Warren) Christopher, Ross and Mr Netanyahu," he said.

"These efforts are a continuation of the Egyptian efforts to achieve a breakthrough, and the result of all these contacts is that his majesty will pay a visit to Tel Aviv to meet Mr Netanyahu," he said.
